notes:
User enjoys healthy, easy meal-prep ideas and is exploring bean- and lentil-based meals. They recently made a delicious chili con carne and wanted similar recipes. Ideas discussed included Black Bean and Sweet Potato Enchiladas, Cuban Black Bean and Rice Bowl, White Bean and Spinach Stew, red lentil curry, lentil vegetable stew, lentil-mushroom bolognese, vegan chili, bean/lentil chili, and refried beans.

User plans to make a Cuban Black Bean and Rice Bowl with black beans, onions, bell peppers, garlic, brown rice, avocado, and lime. They also recently bought an Air Fryer and want crispy sweet potato fries as a side. Suggested Air Fryer method: cut uniform thin fries, soak in cold water at least 30 minutes, dry thoroughly, lightly oil, cook at 400°F/200°C for roughly 12–15 minutes, shaking the basket halfway, and cooking in batches to avoid overcrowding. Season after cooking if using salt or delicate spices.

For dessert, user chose a simple, refreshing fruit salad. It can include strawberries, grapes, kiwi, pineapple, or their preferred fruits, with lime juice, a little sugar, and optional mint. Other options mentioned were coconut-lime yogurt parfait and banana nice cream.

User asked about storing leftovers. Cuban Black Bean and Rice Bowl components can be refrigerated in shallow, airtight containers within 2 hours of cooking and generally used within 3–4 days (up to 5 days under standard food-safety guidance). For longer storage, cool promptly and freeze in airtight, dated, portioned containers; thaw safely in the refrigerator and reheat to 165°F/74°C. Rice can dry out, so a small amount of water or broth may help when reheating.

For sweet potato fries, do not store them in a pantry or leave them at room temperature. Refrigerate promptly in an airtight container, preferably with a paper towel, and use within about 1–2 days; they will soften. For longer storage, cool and freeze promptly in a single layer, then transfer once frozen to a sealed freezer container or bag. Reheat from frozen in the Air Fryer or oven until hot and crisp, ensuring the center is thoroughly heated. A brief reheating restores texture better than refrigeration.

User also owns a new Instant Pot and is interested in healthy lunches and pressure-cooked soups/stews, especially Korean Chicken Stew (Jjimdak). Their intended adaptations are:
- Boneless, skinless chicken breast cut into bite-size pieces instead of thighs/drumsticks.
- Reduce gochugaru/Korean chili flakes from 2 Tbsp to 1 Tbsp because they are unfamiliar with gochujang and concerned about heat; season and adjust after tasting.
- Ingredients: chicken breast, potatoes, carrots, onion, garlic, gochujang, soy sauce, gochugaru, brown sugar, black pepper, chicken broth, sesame oil, and optional green onions.
- Chicken breast may be drier and may require a shorter pressure-cooking time than thighs/drumsticks.
